title: 6 West Charge Nurse: 19 Beds, Only 2 With a Door

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge
transcript.text: Command center, this is Angela, charge on 6 West. I've just walked every room. I can give the ICU 24 telemetry beds, but only 2 of them are private rooms with a door. The other 22 are semi-private bays.

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge
transcript.text: And I still have 4 med-surg patients in those beds. I can't move them until 7 West takes them, and 7 West is full of NICU right now. So, realistically, I can take 17 ICU patients in bays plus 2 isolation rooms. That's 19, but only if every one of them fits a bay.

transcript.speaker: CNO
transcript.text: Understood, Angela. Stay on. Dr. Anil Chaudhary is here with me.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anil Chaudhary
transcript.text: 3-11 and 3-18 are on contact isolation with different organisms. They get the 2 private rooms, and nobody cohorts them. That leaves 17 bays for 17 patients.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anil Chaudhary
transcript.text: Two of those 17 are 3-07, on 3 pressors, and 3-14, who's proned. Moving 3-14 means unproning him in a hallway. I'd rather keep both on floor 3 with a vent team.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anil Chaudhary
transcript.text: But floor 3 will be on its own at 1:3 when the ground floor floods. No pharmacy runs, no imaging, and the elevators may be gone by then.

transcript.speaker: 6 West Charge
transcript.text: If they stay, I'd hold two bays empty so I'm not turning anyone away later. Just tell me which way. I'm setting up the bays now.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Anil Chaudhary
transcript.text: You decide. 3-07 and 3-14 come up to 6 West now, or they stay on 3 with their own team. I need an answer before the ICU elevator slot at 09:30.
